sub_scenario.family: physical constraint versus sustained work commitment
sub_scenario.one_line: conference interpreter: booth weeks above the escort circuit

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the booth console and closing stale entries.
The assignment calendar review wrapped early today.
Escort interpreting for a two-hour ceremony is fine; short standing stints cost nothing.
Someone new shadowed me in the interpreting booth this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the session rotations into one message before lunch.
At the trade summit I worked the seated booth with thirty-minute partner rotations, and my output stayed clean through six full days.
It carries anyone, but my hip especially.
Seated consecutive interpreting at dinners runs long but never hurts.
Seated formats are safe regardless of length.
I archived last cycle's notes on the assignment calendar and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
My hip physiotherapy runs twice a week all season; the therapist flagged prolonged standing as the one thing that undoes the progress.
A vendor call about the booth console ran long but ended well.
I walked through the interpreting booth checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the session rotations.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the assignment calendar records and fixed it at the source.
The factory-tour escort circuit is four to six hours on your feet per visit, moving through production halls, and my one escort week last year ended with a flare that cost me two booth days.
The escort format triggered it directly.
I sketched next week's plan for the session rotations before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the booth console updates.
The booth client is a repeat contract; the escort circuit pays slightly more per day but books irregularly.
Close enough that fit should decide it.
The agency coordinator keeps saying escort work is where interpreters become indispensable to clients.
I closed the week by updating the interpreting booth handover notes.
The agency asks which assignment block to lock first for spring: booth weeks or the factory-tour escort circuit. What do I put first?
